key_insight: A 145,281-parameter multi-head quantum module replaced eight transformer blocks in a 30-billion-parameter LLM, displacing 16.33% of its parameters with little reported accuracy loss.
engineering_relevance: Partitioning hidden states into small quantum heads enables NISQ-compatible integration into a production-scale LLM without encoding its full width in one circuit.
method: Partition 2,048 hidden dimensions into 32 heads using 8-qubit registers and angle encoding.
Process heads with quantum circuits and learned readouts, coupled through constrained classical linear mixers.
Train with exact statevector simulation, then execute fusion-checkpoint quantum heads on a 156-qubit IBM Heron processor.
evidence_signal: Held-out perplexity ablations found mixers alone within 1–3% of the full module for fused spans, while a parameter-matched classical MLP remained a few percent ahead.
watch_item: A benefit specific to trained, entangling circuits is unproven: limited-seed non-entangling and frozen-circuit controls outperformed the full module, and training used classical simulation.
paper_title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
